title: Going Places and Doing Activities with Go
summary: Learn when to say go to, go on, go for and go + -ing. Use these patterns to talk about destinations, trips and everyday activities.
learningObjectives: Use go to for destinations and recognise go home without to.
Choose go on for holidays, tours, trips, cruises and strikes.
Use go for + an activity noun and go + -ing for common leisure activities.
Distinguish go to bed and go to sleep from go home.

explanation.heading: Go to a place; go home without to
explanation.body: Use go to before many destinations, such as the office, a concert or the dentist. Use go to bed when you go to your bed to rest, and go to sleep for the moment you begin sleeping. Home is an exception: say go home, with no to.
explanation.example: After the film, Nina went home and went to bed.

explanation.heading: Go on for holidays and organised events
explanation.body: Use go on with a holiday, a trip, a tour or a cruise. Go on strike means that workers stop working as a protest. These are fixed combinations; do not replace on with to or for.
explanation.example: Our neighbours are going on a walking tour tomorrow.

explanation.heading: Go for an activity expressed as a noun
explanation.body: Use go for before noun phrases such as a walk, a run, a swim, a drink or a meal. You can add a destination: go for a walk in the park. The article a is part of many of these expressions.
explanation.example: After lunch, we went for a short walk by the river.

explanation.heading: Go + -ing for sports and shopping
explanation.body: Use go + an -ing verb for activities such as swimming, skiing, fishing, cycling and shopping. You can change the tense of go: we go swimming, we went swimming, she is going shopping. Do not add to or for before the -ing form in this pattern.
explanation.example: My brother goes cycling on Sunday mornings.

comparisons.title: Go to a destination, but go home

left.label: Go to + place
left.example: I go to the library after work.
left.note: Use to before the destination the library.

right.label: Go home
right.note: Home follows go directly; do not say to home.

left.label: Go for + noun
left.note: A swim is an activity expressed as a noun.

right.label: Go + -ing
right.note: Swimming is the -ing activity form; both sentences invite the same activity.

examples.sentence: Leila went to the theatre with her parents.
We went home before it started raining.
examples.note: There is no preposition before home.

examples.sentence: The class is going on a day trip next Thursday.
examples.note: Go on is the normal pattern for a trip.

examples.sentence: Shall we go for a drink after the match?
examples.note: Go for + a drink names a social activity.

examples.sentence: I sometimes go fishing with my grandfather.
examples.note: Go + -ing describes a hobby or leisure activity.

commonMistakes.incorrect: I need to go to home now.
commonMistakes.correct: I need to go home now.
commonMistakes.why: Go home does not take the preposition to.

commonMistakes.incorrect: We are going for holiday in July.
commonMistakes.correct: We are going on holiday in July.
commonMistakes.why: The usual expression is go on holiday.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Do you want to go for shopping?
commonMistakes.correct: Do you want to go shopping?
commonMistakes.why: With shopping, use go + -ing without for.

commonMistakes.incorrect: They went on a walk after breakfast.
commonMistakes.correct: They went for a walk after breakfast.
commonMistakes.why: Use go for a walk when walk is a noun.

studyTips: Learn the go patterns as short chunks: go to the office; go on holiday; go for a run; go swimming.
Contrast noun and activity forms: go for a swim, but go swimming. Never use go for swimming for this meaning.
Remember the special endings: go home, go to bed and go to sleep.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: Mina goes ___ school by bicycle.
exercises.feedback: School is the destination, so the usual expression is goes to school.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: The airport workers have gone ___ strike.
exercises.feedback: The fixed expression for stopping work as a protest is go on strike.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence correctly describes a regular weekend activity?
choices: We go for shopping every Saturday.
We go to shopping every Saturday.
exercises.feedback: Shopping follows go directly as an -ing activity: go shopping.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence about returning to your house.
choices: We went home after the show.
We went to home after the show.
We went on home after the show.
exercises.feedback: Home follows the verb go without to or on.

exercises.prompt: After dinner, Alex went ___ bed because he was tired.
acceptedAnswers: to
exercises.feedback: The fixed destination expression is go to bed.

exercises.prompt: Every August, my neighbours go ___ holiday for two weeks.
acceptedAnswers: on
exercises.feedback: Holiday is used with go on: go on holiday.

exercises.prompt: We went ___ a short walk around the lake.
acceptedAnswers: for
exercises.feedback: A walk is a noun phrase; use go for a walk.

exercises.prompt: Complete with the -ing form of ski: They go ___ in the mountains every winter.
acceptedAnswers: skiing
exercises.feedback: For this sport, use go + -ing: go skiing.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: I am going to home straight after class.
acceptedAnswers: I am going home straight after class.
I'm going home straight after class.
exercises.feedback: Go home has no to before home.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: My parents went in a cruise last summer.
acceptedAnswers: My parents went on a cruise last summer.
exercises.feedback: Use go on a cruise for this kind of holiday.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence using the word swimming: We went for swimming before lunch.
acceptedAnswers: We went swimming before lunch.
exercises.feedback: Use go + -ing without for: went swimming.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Shall we go on a meal after the concert?
acceptedAnswers: Shall we go for a meal after the concert?
exercises.feedback: A meal is an activity noun here, so use go for a meal.

speakingExercises.prompt: Make one complete sentence in the past simple from these cues: Theo / go / to the dentist / yesterday.
acceptedAnswers: Theo went to the dentist yesterday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Went to the dentist is the past form of go to + destination.

speakingExercises.prompt: Use the present continuous and on in a complete sentence: We / go / on holiday / next week.
acceptedAnswers: We're going on holiday next week.
We are going on holiday next week.
speakingExercises.feedback: Going on holiday uses on after go and the present continuous for a plan.

speakingExercises.prompt: Make a complete present simple sentence: The children / go swimming / every Sunday.
acceptedAnswers: The children go swimming every Sunday.
speakingExercises.feedback: For a repeated activity, use the present simple go swimming.

speakingExercises.prompt: Use these cues to make one present-simple sentence: Zoe / go to bed / at nine / every night.
acceptedAnswers: Zoe goes to bed at nine every night.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use goes to bed for Zoe’s nightly routine. Go to bed takes to, unlike go home.

speakingExercises.prompt: Change this sentence to the past simple, keeping the other words: “My uncle goes for a walk after lunch.”
acceptedAnswers: My uncle went for a walk after lunch.
speakingExercises.feedback: Change goes to went, and keep the expression for a walk.

speakingExercises.prompt: A friend asks, “Where does the coach go after practice?” You know the coach returns home. Answer with one sentence beginning “The coach”.
acceptedAnswers: The coach goes home after practice.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use goes home without to. The coach is singular, so use goes.

speakingExercises.prompt: Correct the preposition in this sentence about an organised city tour, without changing anything else: “We went to a city tour yesterday.”
acceptedAnswers: We went on a city tour yesterday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use go on a tour. Go for is used with activities such as a walk or a swim.

speakingExercises.prompt: Invite a friend to go for a swim at the lake tomorrow morning. Begin with “Let’s”, use the expression “go for a swim”, and include the place and time.
acceptedAnswers: Let's go for a swim at the lake tomorrow morning.
Let's go for a swim tomorrow morning at the lake.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use let’s go for a swim, with for before the activity noun a swim.

listeningExercises.audioText: We're going on a boat trip tomorrow morning.
listeningExercises.prompt: What is planned for tomorrow morning?
listeningExercises.feedback: The speaker says they are going on a boat trip.

listeningExercises.audioText: After breakfast, Lewis went for a run in the park.
listeningExercises.prompt: What did Lewis do after breakfast?
listeningExercises.feedback: Went for a run names the activity Lewis did.

listeningExercises.audioText: It's late, so I'm going home now.
listeningExercises.prompt: Complete what you hear: “It’s late, so I’m going ___ now.” Type only the missing word.
acceptedAnswers: home
listeningExercises.feedback: Go home uses no to; the word heard is home.

listeningExercises.audioText: We went to the bakery early to buy rolls for breakfast.
listeningExercises.prompt: Why did the people visit the shop?
choices: To buy tickets for a show.
To meet a friend for lunch.
To get food for a morning meal.
listeningExercises.feedback: They visited a bakery to buy food for breakfast. Went to introduces the destination.

listeningExercises.audioText: On Saturdays, Felix goes cycling by the river, but his sister goes shopping in town.
listeningExercises.prompt: Who does a sport on Saturdays?
listeningExercises.feedback: Felix cycles, which is a sport; his sister shops. Both activities use go plus -ing.

listeningExercises.audioText: After the late film, Grace went home, but her cousin went to bed at the guesthouse.
choices: Both people returned to their own homes.
Grace returned home while her cousin stayed at the guesthouse.
Grace went to sleep at the guesthouse.
listeningExercises.feedback: Went home describes Grace’s return, while her cousin went to bed at another place.

listeningExercises.audioText: Next spring, my parents are going on a cruise around the islands.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the three words you hear immediately after “going”.
acceptedAnswers: on a cruise
listeningExercises.feedback: Go on a cruise is the standard expression for this kind of trip.

listeningExercises.audioText: In summer, we often go for a swim in the lake after work.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the three words you hear immediately after “go”.
acceptedAnswers: for a swim
listeningExercises.feedback: For a swim is an activity noun phrase after go; go swimming is another correct pattern.
